title: The role of Alu elements in causing BRCA1 structural variation and breast cancer susceptibility.
authors: Yu, Minjae; Jo, Dahee; Shin, Wonseok; Han, Kyudong
one_liner_zh: 该文综述Alu元件导致BRCA1结构变异与乳腺癌易感性，聚焦基因组结构变异检测与临床意义，未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作建模或TF-DNA结合机制，仅提及机器学习预测工具，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BRCA1 is a tumor suppressor gene encoding a protein which plays an essential role in the repair of DNA double strand break. Approximately 40% of its introns are composed of Alu elements. It is known that retrotransposons create an environment prone to non-allelic recombination (NAHR) between homologous sequences, which frequently cause deletion or duplication of exon(s) resulting in structural variations in the gene. Some mutations can directly impact protein function by causing frameshifts, the deletion of key domains, and abnormal RNA processing, possibly increasing tumorigenicity. Indeed, large-scale BRCA1 rearrangements caused by Alu elements have been observed in approximately 10-15% of hereditary breast cancer patients, most notably deletions of exons 5 through 7. Occasionally, mutated exons are excluded from splicing, resulting in protein isoforms with a limited function, which may be associated with drug resistance during treatment. Tumors with BRCA1 mutations exhibit homologous recombination deficiency (HRD), resulting in high sensitivity to PARP inhibitors and platinum-based chemotherapy. However, in some tumors, gene function may be partially restored through subsequent secondary rearrangements, which can lead to long-term drug resistance, demanding continuous molecular surveillance. It has been difficult to detect mutations in the BRCA gene caused by Alu elements using conventional PCR-based analysis or short-read next-generation sequencing (NGS) technologies. However, the recent introduction of MLPA and long-read NGS technologies has significantly improved a detection rate of Alu-involved mutations in the BRCA gene. Advances in long-read sequencing technologies, such as Oxford Nanopore and PacBio, and in optical genome mapping tools provide the capability to analyze complex structural mutations. Furthermore, machine learning-based prediction tools, such as HRDetect and SVScore, have been developed to analyze genome-wide structural mutation patterns and HRD indicators more comprehensively, thereby contributing to the prediction of BRCA1/2 defects and treatment responses. The integration of these technologies is expected to enhance our comprehension of BRCA1-related structural mutations and serve as an important foundation for developing personalized treatment strategies for patients.
abstract_zh: BRCA1是一种肿瘤抑制基因，编码的蛋白质在DNA双链断裂修复中发挥关键作用。其约40%的内含子由Alu元件组成。已知逆转录转座子营造了同源序列间易发生非等位重组（NAHR）的环境，这常导致外显子缺失或重复，从而引起基因的结构变异。某些突变可通过导致移码、关键结构域缺失及异常RNA加工直接影响蛋白质功能，可能增加致瘤性。事实上，由Alu元件引起的大规模BRCA1重排已在约10-15%的遗传性乳腺癌患者中观察到，最显著的是外显子5至7的缺失。偶尔，突变的外显子被排除在剪接之外，产生功能受限的蛋白质异构体，这可能与治疗期间的药物耐药性相关。携带BRCA1突变的肿瘤表现出同源重组缺陷（HRD），导致对PARP抑制剂和铂类化疗高度敏感。然而，在某些肿瘤中，基因功能可能通过随后的次级重排部分恢复，这可能导致长期耐药性，需要持续的分子监测。使用基于PCR的传统分析或短读长下一代测序（NGS）技术检测由Alu元件引起的BRCA基因突变一直较为困难。然而，MLPA和长读长NGS技术的近期引入显著提高了BRCA基因中涉及Alu的突变检出率。长读长测序技术（如Oxford Nanopore和PacBio）以及光学基因组作图的进展提供了分析复杂结构突变的能力。此外，基于机器学习的预测工具（如HRDetect和SVScore）已被开发，用于更全面地分析全基因组结构突变模式和HRD指标，从而有助于预测BRCA1/2缺陷和治疗反应。这些技术的整合预计将增强我们对BRCA1相关结构突变的理解，并为患者制定个性化治疗策略提供重要基础。
